text:
Priya: paging — incident bot flagged high GPU utilization in dedicated pool helixbank-prod-pool, single tenant (HelixBank) causing token generation errors. getting alerted to 95%+ GPU mem and queuing. @Liam you oncall? :rotating_light:
Liam: I'm on it. seeing the same in metrics. All nodes in helixbank-prod-pool show sustained <10% free GPU memory, pending queue length rising. panic? no, but latency breach for their SLAs.
IncidentBot: AUTOMATED ALERT: dedicated-pool-usage > 90% for helixbank-prod-pool (tenant=HelixBank). Triggered at 03:05 UTC.
Priya: quick context — HelixBank is on dedicated reserved pool with burst capacity disabled (policy locked for compliance). They are hitting a sudden traffic spike from a fraud-detection batch kickoff.
Evan: paste of redwoodctl output: ```
redwoodctl pools describe helixbank-prod-pool --json
{
  "allocated_gpus": 16,
  "in_use_gpus": 16,
  "queued_requests": 42,
  "avg_latency_ms": 720,
  "burst_enabled": false
}
```
Liam: looks like we're at hard capacity. Options: 1) enable burst into shared spare capacity (needs acct approval + potential isolation risk), 2) preempt lower-priority HelixBank jobs (they have some nightly batch jobs we can throttle), 3) failover requests to hosted model variant (but customer data restrictions may block), 4) spin up temporary dedicated nodes in their VPC - long lead time.
Sofia: FYI billing/account — HelixBank has a committed reserved plan but no active burst add-on. We can provision emergency burst charge, they will be invoiced, but need AC from account exec. I can ping AE now.
Priya: immediate mitigation first: can we identify non-critical HelixBank workloads to preempt? Evan, any labeling we can use?
Evan: yes, label is "priority:low" on nightly-derivative jobs. I can run a quick script to pause those. Command: ```
redwoodctl jobs list --pool helixbank-prod-pool --filter "priority:low" --format id
# then
redwoodctl jobs pause <id>
```
Liam: do it. preempting tenant-internal low-priority jobs avoids cross-tenant mixing. do it now.
Evan: pausing 8 jobs now... paused 8 low-priority jobs. queued_requests dropped from 42 -> 18, avg_latency -> 380ms and GPU mem freed ~22%.
Priya: updating status to HelixBank support channel: "We observed a sudden spike; preempted non-critical jobs to restore SLA. Investigating root cause and coordinating with account team on burst options." 
Support-Bot: Created support ticket TICKET-5842 for HelixBank. Notified account exec @Sofia.
Sofia: I pinged AE and legal for a one-time burst approval. AE responded "approve if customer signs surge bill; legal to confirm isolation requirements." They asked for an estimate of cost and duration. Liam, any numbers?
Liam: estimate: 4 extra vGPUs for ~3 hours = approx $2.6k on demand. If we enable cross-tenant burst, risk profile increases — need encryption in transit assurances; legal may block.
Priya: what's tradeoff of enabling hosted fallback (model variant hosted-redwood-small)?
Evan: hosted fallback is feasible only if HelixBank allows data to leave their dedicated pool (they have a strict VPC-only clause). The contract clause says no cross-tenant compute, so hosted fallback is a no-go without exec sign-off.
Priya: okay we can't move traffic offsite. Next step: can we autoscale in their VPC quickly? Any infra automation?
Evan: we have a terraform module to spin up dedicated nodes in customer VPC but it takes ~18-25 minutes once credentials are provided and subnet/enis are available. We can start that and keep preemptions active.
Liam: start the infra spin-up now as parallel path. I'll keep preemption in place until new nodes come online.
Priya: Evan, execute and paste logs here. Also create a K8s drain plan for graceful migration.
Evan: launching infra: ```
terraform apply -var="tenant=helixbank" -auto-approve
> queued tasks: create-instance(4 x a100-80gb), attach-nics, register-with-pool
```
Evan: 6 minutes in: instances provisioning. health checks pending.
Priya: good. I'll go to customer comms: "We've preempted lower-priority jobs and are provisioning temporary capacity. No data left the VPC. We'll update when capacity is added." @Sofia can you confirm messaging/escrow of surcharges?
Sofia: confirm. I've drafted a note to AE to get customer approval to bill for emergency burst. They replied 'proceed and we'll reconcile'. Keeping them in the loop.
IncidentBot: UPDATE: pool utilisation dropped to 68% after preemptions. new nodes expected in ~12 minutes.
Liam: monitoring logs: some requests still failing at 503 due to queue timeout. short-term configuration: increase request timeout to 25s for HelixBank route to reduce 503 rate, will trade latency. `redwoodctl routes update helixbank-route --timeout 25s`.
Priya: go ahead, but record that change as temporary. Evan, do apply.
Evan: applied route timeout increase. 503s dropping, p90 latency still high but SLOs for error rate restored.
Priya: handoff plan for next oncall (Liam -> next):
- preemptions remain active until new nodes are fully registered and warm.
- infra task id: terraform-run-helix-1768501234 (monitor cloud console).
- support ticket TICKET-5842 open, AE confirmed provisional approval for billing surge.
- do NOT enable cross-tenant burst without legal sign-off.
- next action: if new nodes not up in 25 minutes, escalate to infra lead (Evan) for manual bailout.
Liam: I'll take the oncall for next 2h. summary: mitigated by pausing low-priority tenant jobs and provisioning temporary capacity.
Sofia: I'll follow up with AE + customer postmortem note and cost details.
Support-Bot: TICKET-5842 updated with mitigation steps and estimated costs.
Evan: new nodes registered at +14m, pool capacity increased to 20 gpus, queued_requests drained. Performing warmup of model shards; KV caches warming. latency returning to baseline 120ms.
Priya: great. closing incident once we confirm stability for 30m and queue cleared. final checklist for postmortem: root cause of HelixBank batch kickoff, why autoscale burst was disabled, look at policy exception flow, and make a runbook for one-time emergency burst approvals.
Liam: adding runbook task to eng-sre backlog and assigning to me.
Priya: thank you all. reactions: :thumbsup: :white_check_mark:
Sofia: adding customer comms note to ticket and flagging for account review.
Priya: handing off to @Liam oncall. ending thread.
